chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Abdullah ibn Muhraz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'A man left behind his daughter and a sister of his father and mother.' He said, 'All the wealth is for the daughter, and there is nothing for the sister of the father and mother.'

key_terms.الذين share one parent with the deceased: his sister, [who is] from his father and mother (full sister)
key_terms.لِأَبِيهِ وَ أُمِّهِ: of his father and mother (indicating half-siblings)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits when a deceased leaves a daughter and sisters?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'blocking' (hajb) in Shia inheritance jurisprudence, where the presence of a daughter excludes both paternal and maternal half-sisters from receiving any share. It highlights the distinct treatment of siblings based on their lineage relative to the deceased, a key topic in the science of fara'id (inheritance distribution).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Abdullah Bin Muhraz, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man left his daughter and a sister of his father, and his mother’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wealth, all of it is for the daughter, and there is nothing for the sister of the father, and the mother’.
en.sarwar: 8. Afi ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhriz who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who dies and leaves behind his daughter and his sister from his mother and father.
He (the Imam) said, ‘The legacy belongs to his daughter and there is nothing for his sister from his mother and father.’”
